hints.junior: Nothing about the animation code changed — left just can't move without the browser recomputing layout and repainting, and both need the main thread the heavy work is occupying.
hints.mid: Layout properties (width, height, top, left) force layout + paint + composite every frame; transform and opacity can skip straight to compositing.
hints.staff: Transform/opacity changes can be handled entirely by the compositor thread — structurally independent of the main thread, not just cheaper.

hints.junior: Click 'Block main thread' and watch closely — the left-animated box freezes for the block's duration, while the transform box keeps sliding.
hints.mid: Broken animates left with a CSS keyframe loop; fixed animates transform: translateX() with the same timing and distance. The block button runs a real synchronous busy-loop.
hints.staff: This is a live compositor-thread demonstration — the transform animation genuinely keeps progressing during the busy-loop because it never needed the blocked main thread to compute the next frame.

hints.junior: Changing left means the browser doesn't know where anything ends up until it reruns layout — every frame, all three pipeline stages. Changing transform skips straight to the cheapest one, compositing.
hints.mid: "Stick to compositor-only properties": express a slide as translate, a resize as scale, a fade as opacity, wherever the visual result allows it.
hints.staff: Because compositor animations don't need the main thread per frame, they keep running during a busy main thread — a layout-property animation has no such independence and simply loses frames under load.

hints.junior: will-change: transform hints the browser to prepare a compositor layer ahead of time — a targeted tool, not a default to sprinkle everywhere.
hints.mid: Not every visual change has a compositor-only equivalent — an accordion genuinely pushing content down can't be faked with transform alone.
hints.staff: Some properties assumed to be 'layout' are actually paint-only (background-color, box-shadow) — cheaper than layout but still not compositor-only. Apply will-change via JS just before animating and remove it after.

sections.junior: Today's case is about a progress bar that looked perfectly smooth on an idle page, and then visibly froze the moment the app actually had real work to do on the main thread.
sections.mid: Not every CSS property costs the same to animate — layout properties force the browser to redo layout and paint on every frame, while transform and opacity don't.
sections.staff: The sharper version is that transform and opacity changes can run entirely on a thread separate from the one running your JavaScript, which is why they can keep going even while that thread is fully blocked.

sections.junior: The browser turns a frame into pixels through layout, paint, and composite. Changing left forces all three, every frame. Changing transform skips straight to the cheapest one.
sections.mid: Stick to compositor only properties. A slide is a translate, a resize is a scale, a fade is opacity, wherever the visual result allows it.
sections.staff: The independence from the main thread is the part worth remembering precisely. A layout property animation has no such independence, so under load it simply loses frames.

sections.junior: Try clicking the block main thread button and watch what happens to each moving box.
sections.mid: One box is animated with left, the other with transform. Watch which one keeps moving once the main thread gets busy.
sections.staff: This is a real compositor thread demonstration running in your browser, not a simulated difference.

sections.junior: Animating left, top, width, or height forces the browser to redo layout every frame, and it stutters under load. Animating transform or opacity skips that entirely.
sections.mid: Express slides as translate, resizes as scale, and fades as opacity wherever you can, for a fraction of the rendering cost.
sections.staff: Compositor only animations run independently of the main thread, which is why they stay smooth under real load where layout property animations visibly drop frames.
